meta.projectName: P0 LLM Service Hardening - David's Goliath

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down the initialization process into: (1) Set up Node.js and package manager, (2) Scaffold project with Vite or Vue CLI, (3) Install and configure Ionic Vue, (4) Set up ESLint, Prettier, and Husky, (5) Configure mobile-first responsiveness, (6) Verify build, lint, and emulator tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Project initialization is moderately complex due to the integration of multiple tools (Vue 3, Ionic, ESLint, Prettier, Husky) and the need for mobile-first configuration and code quality tooling. Each step is standard but requires careful sequencing and verification for a robust foundation.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into: (1) Install and configure Pinia, (2) Set up root store, (3) Create modular stores for each domain (PII patterns, pseudonym dictionaries, LLM monitoring, analytics), (4) Define TypeScript interfaces, (5) Write unit tests for store logic.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Integrating Pinia with modular stores and TypeScript interfaces adds complexity, especially with alignment to backend models and ensuring type safety. Testing and modularization are best practices that warrant explicit subtasks.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Set Up Axios API Service Layer
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Decompose into: (1) Install Axios, (2) Create base service module with environment config, (3) Implement typed endpoint methods, (4) Add error interceptors and retry logic, (5) Write unit tests for API service.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Centralizing API logic with error handling, retries, and type safety is a common but non-trivial pattern. Proper separation and testing are essential for maintainability and reliability.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into: (1) Create ErrorBoundary component using errorCaptured, (2) Integrate with Pinia for global error state, (3) Implement fallback UI and recovery options, (4) Add error logging for audit trail, (5) Test error scenarios and UI.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Global error handling requires careful integration with state management, UI, and logging. Ensuring graceful degradation and actionable recovery increases complexity beyond basic error capture.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into: (1) Design table layout with Ionic components, (2) Implement sorting and filtering, (3) Add real-time search, (4) Enable bulk actions (enable/disable/delete), (5) Add visual indicators for pattern types, (6) Connect to Pinia and Axios, (7) Write unit and integration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This component is feature-rich, requiring advanced UI logic, state synchronization, and robust testing. Bulk actions and real-time updates add to the complexity.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into: (1) Add new privacy metrics (detection counts, pseudonymization, redaction), (2) Implement data classification display, (3) Add expandable before/after text view, (4) Integrate cost breakdown and performance impact, (5) Connect to API and Pinia, (6) Write unit and integration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Enhancing an existing panel with multiple new metrics, dynamic views, and API/state integration is moderately complex and requires careful UI and data handling.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Decompose into: (1) Design undo/redo stack or use Pinia plugin, (2) Integrate with PIIPatternEditor, (3) Integrate with PseudonymDictionaryManager, (4) Implement UI controls, (5) Persist changes only on confirmation, (6) Write unit and integration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Undo/redo logic is inherently complex due to state history management, UI integration, and ensuring data consistency across multiple components.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into: (1) Enforce HTTPS in Axios config, (2) Validate and sanitize user inputs, (3) Integrate DOMPurify for input sanitization, (4) Write security and unit tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Security tasks are critical and require careful configuration and validation, but the implementation steps are well-defined and follow established patterns.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Access Control for Admin Features
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into: (1) Integrate Supabase Auth for authentication, (2) Implement role-based access logic, (3) Protect routes and components with navigation guards, (4) Sync access state with Pinia, (5) Write unit and integration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Role-based access control involves authentication, route protection, and state synchronization, all of which require careful coordination and thorough testing.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into: (1) Detect API failures globally, (2) Display user-friendly error messages, (3) Suggest recovery steps, (4) Enable offline editing for patterns, (5) Implement change queue for later sync, (6) Test fallback and offline scenarios.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Graceful degradation with offline support and queued changes is complex, requiring global error detection, robust UI, and reliable offline data handling.
